comparator.name: Cognitive Science and Artificial Intelligence
comparator.sourceNotes: English full-time BSc, September-2026 entrant curriculum. Ten six-credit units in each earlier year and thirty credits of final-year mobility plus three six-credit subjects and a twelve-credit thesis total 180 EC. The public first-listed exchange option is retained without inventing a destination. The adopted appendix explicitly gives the 2027–2028 second year and 2028–2029 third year for this cohort; Hybrid Intelligence replaces Knowledge Representation. GROW is a zero-credit development trajectory. Research Workshop entry requires the stated first-year thinking/statistics courses and ten participant-pool hours; advanced programming and machine learning require earlier programming, with statistics also required for machine learning. Thesis entry requires all first-year courses plus sixty postpropaedeutic credits and no start before semester six. Earlier complete years meet these conditions. The exchange package remains subject to Board approval and ordinary academic/non-overlap/admission conditions; no internship is imposed.

components.name: Introduction to Machine Learning
components.note: Entry requires Statistics for CSAI I and either Introduction to Programming or Data Structures and Algorithms.

components.name: Advanced Programming for CSAI
components.note: Entry requires at least one of the earlier programming courses. Functional, concurrent and object-oriented programming build on those foundations.

components.name: Research Workshop: CSAI
components.note: A group project covers the research cycle through an experiment or a machine-learning study. Entry requires Critical and Scientific Thinking, Statistics for CSAI I and ten hours in the human subject pool.

components.name: Exchange/Study Abroad
components.note: Thirty credits are reserved for approved study at a partner university. The destination and courses remain open. The package must meet entry, academic quality, coherence and non-overlap requirements.

components.name: BSc Thesis CSAI
components.note: The twelve-credit thesis is a supervised empirical quantitative study in cognitive science and artificial intelligence, including programming, analysis and academic reporting. Entry requires all first-year courses and at least sixty later-year credits. It cannot start before semester six.

progressionAssessment.rationale: All assigned-term offerings and earlier formal prerequisites pass. Programming precedes image processing; data workflows precede machine learning and machine learning precedes deep learning. Brain foundations precede advanced cognitive courses. In the computational option, methods precedes behavioural statistics and algorithms precedes advanced algorithms.

basisLabels: Cognition, psychology, neuroscience, perception and learning
courseTraceability.rationale: Introduction to Brain & Behavior directly introduces neuropsychology, neural signalling, learning and research methods, providing a biological and behavioural foundation for cognitive AI questions. It implements the explicit academic basis “Cognition, psychology, neuroscience, perception and learning”.

basisLabels: Mathematics, logic, probability, statistics and data modelling
Experimental design, research methods, academic communication and independent research
courseTraceability.rationale: Introduction to Data Science directly supplies reproducible data cleaning, joining, visualisation and project work in R for the empirical data used by cognitive research and machine learning. It implements the explicit academic basis “Mathematics, logic, probability, statistics and data modelling” and “Experimental design, research methods, academic communication and independent research”.

basisLabels: Programming, algorithms, software and computer systems

basisLabels: Mathematics, logic, probability, statistics and data modelling

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest response combines substantial AI computation with cognition and neuroscience. Computational AI and autonomous systems, followed by cognitive processes, language and neuroscience, each produces a coherent feasible curriculum and a material change of academic priorities meeting the four-course distinctness floor. Responsible and explainable AI is a separate, supported ethical-design direction, not a residual part of the cognitive candidate. It is not constructed after the three-programme maximum; existing ethics and philosophical reflection do not imply dedicated interface design, explainability engineering or sustainability training.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both introduce statistical reasoning, empirical analysis and research data. Tilburg specifically teaches R with chi-square tests, t-tests, ANOVA and regression; UCR adds research design, sampling and a project.

Both apply moral reflection to AI and its consequences for human values and responsibility. UCR connects this to psychological, social and care relationships; Tilburg develops moral theories, justice and philosophy of technology.
Both teach formal reasoning and sets. Tilburg develops truth-functional and first-order logic and natural deduction; UCR places logic within a broader discrete-mathematics programme.

Both use search algorithms to solve AI problems. UCR develops heuristic, adversarial and constrained optimisation more deeply; Tilburg combines this with AI history, philosophy and an introduction to uncertainty.

Both address reinforcement learning and agents learning from experience. UCR concentrates on this strand; Tilburg surveys several further fields, including neural networks, language, vision and robotics.

Both develop functional and object-oriented programming and maintainable software design. Tilburg centres advanced Python, concurrency and design patterns; UCR works across C++ and Haskell with software development practice.
Both study searching, sorting, data structures and algorithm performance. UCR also develops string and graph algorithms and experimental comparison.
Both implement and evaluate machine-learning models for regression, classification and unsupervised learning using Python and related tools.
Both study neural networks, training and practical deep-learning models, including image, sequential and language applications.

Both study robots through perception, action and control. UCR focuses on robot-arm geometry, kinematics and motion planning; Tilburg emphasises cognitive and social robotics and a social autonomous agent.
Both develop Python programming and algorithmic problem solving through variables, conditions, loops, functions and data structures.
Both teach calculus and its quantitative applications. UCR also includes complex numbers, differential equations and dynamic models.
Both develop vectors, matrices, linear spaces, transformations and eigenvalues for quantitative and computational applications.
Both connect attention, memory, emotion, decision and control with neural systems and investigative methods, including practical experiments. Their selected topics and methods differ.
Both examine language acquisition and processing through cognitive, psychological and neural mechanisms. Tilburg additionally reviews cognitive and computational models of language.

Both introduce relationships among cognition, behaviour and brain function. UCR centres neuropsychology; Tilburg integrates this with philosophy, computation, language and other cognitive-science disciplines.
Both analyse relationships in behavioural data using statistical models and R. Tilburg develops generalised and mixed-effect models; UCR adds experimental design and latent-variable analysis.
Critical evaluation supports several selected courses, but none is placed here as the dedicated study of reasoning biases, rationality and philosophy of science.
Human cognition and social interaction provide relevant foundations, but no selected course provides the dedicated interface design, task analysis and usability evaluation taught here.
Probabilistic and multi-agent decisions contribute related ideas, but no selected course centres the design, validation and simulation of agent-based models taught here.
Methods, data projects and evidence synthesis support research. None is counted again as this separate full-cycle group experiment or machine-learning investigation.
Thirty credits remain open for approved partner-university study; no destination or course package is invented.

Learning algorithms and cognitive inquiry provide foundations, but no selected course centres knowledge-based recurrent networks, symbolic explainability and human-in-the-loop collaborative pipelines.

Psycholinguistics and stylistic analysis study human language and meaning. No selected course provides the dedicated tokenisation, tagging, parsing, distributional semantics and NLP implementation taught here.
The supervised empirical quantitative CSAI thesis remains a separate requirement. Optional UCR independent research is shown outside the scheduled 180 credits.

comparator.note: Entry requires at least one of the earlier programming courses. Functional, concurrent and object-oriented programming build on those foundations.
Entry requires Statistics for CSAI I and either Introduction to Programming or Data Structures and Algorithms.

A group project covers the research cycle through an experiment or a machine-learning study. Entry requires Critical and Scientific Thinking, Statistics for CSAI I and ten hours in the human subject pool.
Thirty credits are reserved for approved study at a partner university. The destination and courses remain open. The package must meet entry, academic quality, coherence and non-overlap requirements.

The twelve-credit thesis is a supervised empirical quantitative study in cognitive science and artificial intelligence, including programming, analysis and academic reporting. Entry requires all first-year courses and at least sixty later-year credits. It cannot start before semester six.
